newsitem.title: USA: Calif. job panel to aid people on welfare - governor.
newsitem.headline: Calif. job panel to aid people on welfare - governor.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson on Monday created a state panel to help find work for welfare recipients.
Wilson, a Republican, said the so-called "Job Action Team" would develop specific proposals to create more job opportunities for welfare recipients and improve job placement.

The panel, made up of business leaders from companies throughout the state, would help California to create jobs for an estimated 600,000 people who will lose public assistance in the coming months, Wilson said.

Last week, Wilson signed an executive order directing all state agencies, departments, boards and commissions "to maximize the employment of welfare recipients," and to ensure they have the opportunity to compete for state jobs.
In January, the Republican governor unveiled his welfare reform plans. In line with federal reforms, Wilson's plan sets a state lifetime limit of five years on aid.

But under Wilson's plan, starting from 1998, able-bodied people currently on welfare may only receive aid for a total of 24 months during any 36 month period. New recipients may only receive aid for 12 months during any 24 month period.
Democratic lawmakers have criticized Wilson's plan, accusing him of not doing enough to find jobs for welfare recipients who will be cut off from aid.
